stories.title: Fourteen small games, all new
stories.subtitle: Hand-built puzzles from EqualInformation are arriving on the App Store.
stories.body:
Each one is free to play, supported by ads, with an optional monthly ad-free plan. They share a promise rather than a template: every game has its own rule, its own look and its own pace. Frogs on lily pads, windmills on a Dutch polder, a goat on a rope bridge, a rock pool you garden. Pick the one that sounds like your kind of quiet.

Android versions are on the way; until then the Android buttons read Coming soon.

stories.title: A tide pool you garden instead of fight
stories.subtitle: In Tidepool Keeper you set the light, the current and the food, then watch life take hold.
stories.body:
A tide pool is a tiny world that runs on its own rules. You are its keeper.

There are 73 pools in eight worlds, a new Daily pool each day, and it works fully offline.

stories.title: Guard the cherries, one lane at a time
stories.subtitle: Scarecrow Lane is a bright orchard defence with 120 levels in eight orchards.
stories.body: Birds drift down five lanes toward the trees. Plant a scarecrow to startle them, hang a wind chime to slow them, and keep the fruit on the branches. Sparrows leave after one startle, crows after two. There is a Daily Lane, an endless Evergreen mode and an Almanac of bird field notes.

stories.title: Roll the snow to exactly the right size
stories.subtitle: Flakeroll turns snowman building into a tidy little logic puzzle.
stories.body: Drag a snowball across a toy-village yard: it grows on fresh snow and shrinks in mud, and a ghost snowman shows the size you need. Across ten worlds, ice, powder, slush, gates and wind each change the rule. There are 100 yards, a Daily Yard and the Blizzard Run.

stories.title: Level the beam, stone by stone
stories.subtitle: Pebble Shift is a balance puzzle on a brass scale.
stories.body: A brass scale sits on a velvet-covered cabinet. Around its base runs a ring of slots, and in some of those slots rest polished stones, each one stamped with a weight. The two pans of the scale hang uneven. Your job is quiet and exact: slide the stones around the ring, one step at a time into an empty neighbouring slot, until the beam swings level.
